chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn al-Hasan at-Taymali narrated to me, saying: Muhammad and Ahmad, the sons of al-Hasan, narrated to us, from Ali ibn Ya'qub al-Hashimi, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:

The name of al-Qa'im will be called out, and he will be brought while he is behind the Maqam (Station of Abraham), and it will be said to him: 'Your name has been called out, so what are you waiting for?' Then his hand will be taken and he will be given allegiance.

(He said) Zurara said to me: 'Praise be to Allah, we used to hear that al-Qa'im would be given allegiance unwillingly, and we did not know the reason for his unwillingness, so we learned that it is an unwillingness without sin.'
ai.seo_question: What is the nature of the Imam's hesitation before accepting allegiance during his appearance?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Nu'mani highlights the divine orchestration of the Mahdi's emergence, where the call to his name at the Maqam Ibrahim signifies the transition from occultation to public leadership. Zurara’s clarification resolves a key theological nuance: the Imam’s apparent hesitation is not a defect or reluctance (karah) but a dignified, sinless deliberation, affirming his perfect readiness to assume the caliphate. This event underscores the legitimacy of his authority as divinely appointed rather than merely politically accepted.
